findings.problem: An early independent projection produced a long wire into a late gated sum.
findings.change: Evaluate one consumer-rank topology after existing print fitting and routing.
findings.visual_assessment: The overview is much shorter with no crossings, but it still has turns and long bypass wires. Arrows remain necessary.

findings.problem: Removing crossings can merely create longer, harder-to-follow paths.
findings.change: Keep a fixed 10% area and wire-length ceiling, no font reduction and no label/contact regression.
findings.visual_assessment: The ConvNet alternative removes one crossing but adds about 19% wire length and more turns around the second convolution block. It was rejected; both SVGs are preserved.

findings.problem: Consumer ranks can make a loop-template panel worse.
findings.change: Measure the actual routed candidate and retain the original when conflicts increase.
findings.visual_assessment: TextCNN loop candidate rises from four to seven crossings. No universal superiority of late ranks is claimed.

findings.problem: Some partial structures improve only slightly and at a routing cost.
findings.change: Keep the accepted residual-detail tradeoff explicit.
findings.visual_assessment: Two crossings become one at the same font and physical size, with about 5.3% more wire length. The long residual bypass remains.

findings.problem: Historical fixed-position and byte-identical SVG comparisons cannot describe a later layout change.
findings.change: Archive old implementation and corpus report; create a separate current evidence directory and validate both renderers in isolated VM globals.
findings.visual_assessment: All 1346 external diagrams reproduce the previous SVG byte for byte; two original panels change. The 91 rejected corpus candidates provide negative evidence only.

limits: No external corpus candidate met the improvement gates. External coverage demonstrates preservation and rejection, not positive generalization.
Folded reading order still needs arrows; fewer crossings does not prove aesthetic or algorithmic completeness.
Only one alternative, at most 64 visible edges, no automatic override of manual geometry; denser or wholly novel topologies can remain poor.
Browser bounds checks find overflow, not diagram aesthetics. Dense unseen graphs, novel Python control flow and unresolved kernels remain open concerns.
